title: Witch's Mark cast at Zada with three Goblins out

you: Goblin token 1 (1/1 red Goblin creature token)
Goblin token 2 (1/1 red Goblin creature token)
Goblin token 3 (1/1 red Goblin creature token)
Mountain x2 (both tapped to cast Witch's Mark)

scenario.mana_available: {0} (the {1}{R} to cast Witch's Mark is already paid; no other mana source)

stack.note: cast targeting only Zada, Hedron Grinder

extras.timing: It is your precombat main phase, you are the active player, and the stack was empty when you cast Witch's Mark (cost {1}{R}, already paid). It has just become cast and is on the stack; any abilities that triggered on casting it have not yet been put on the stack.

scenario.question: Witch's Mark is cast with its one target being Zada. How many copies does Zada create, and does EACH copy offer its own optional discard-a-card-then-draw-two and create its own Wicked Role on its own target? With two other cards in hand, how many cards can you draw in total?

steps.action: Casting Witch's Mark (precombat main phase, you are the active player, stack empty, so sorcery timing is satisfied). You move it from hand to the stack (hand: 3 -> 2, the two Mountains). Its 'up to one target creature you control' is a variable number of targets: you announce ONE target, then announce Zada, Hedron Grinder as that target. You then activate the mana abilities of the two Mountains on the battlefield (both become tapped) and pay the total cost {1}{R}.
steps.effect: Witch's Mark is on the stack targeting only Zada. Mana pool empty; no other mana source. Hand: Mountain, Mountain.

citations.quote: A player who has priority may cast a sorcery card from their hand during a main phase of their turn when the stack is empty.
To propose the casting of a spell, a player first moves that card (or that copy of a card) from where it is to the stack.
If the spell has a variable number of targets, the player announces how many targets they will choose before they announce those targets.
If the total cost includes a mana payment, the player then has a chance to activate mana abilities (see rule 605, “Mana Abilities”). Mana abilities must be activated before costs are paid.
The player pays the total cost.

steps.action: The spell becomes cast. It targets only Zada, so Zada's cast trigger triggers at this moment.
steps.effect: Zada's triggered ability is waiting to be put on the stack above Witch's Mark. (Official ruling agrees: Zada triggers on an instant or sorcery that targets only Zada and no other object or player.)

citations.quote: Any abilities that trigger when a spell is cast or put onto the stack trigger at this time.
Whenever a game event or game state matches a triggered ability’s trigger event, that ability automatically triggers. The ability doesn’t do anything at this point.

steps.action: Before you receive priority, state-based actions are checked (none apply) and Zada's trigger is put on the stack.
steps.effect: Stack, bottom to top: Witch's Mark (targeting Zada), Zada's trigger.

citations.quote: If any state-based actions are performed as a result of a check, the check is repeated; otherwise all triggered abilities that are waiting to be put on the stack are put on the stack, then the check is repeated.
Once an ability has triggered, its controller puts it on the stack as an object that’s not a card the next time a player would receive priority.

steps.action: All players pass priority; Zada's trigger resolves. 'Each other creature you control that the spell could target' is the three Goblin tokens (each a creature you control, a legal target for 'target creature you control'). One copy of Witch's Mark is created per token.
steps.effect: THREE copies are put on the stack above the original, one targeting each Goblin token, in the order you choose. The copies are not cast, so Zada does not trigger again. The trigger then leaves the stack.

citations.quote: Each time all players pass in succession, the spell or ability on top of the stack resolves.
Some effects copy a spell or ability for each player or object it “could target.” The copies are put onto the stack with those targets in the order of their controller’s choice.
a copy of a spell isn’t cast
As the final part of an ability’s resolution, the ability is removed from the stack and ceases to exist.

steps.action: Each copy is a full Witch's Mark spell. Its target (one token) is copied from the trigger's assignment; its 'You may discard a card' choice is NOT copied, because it is a choice made on resolution, so each copy offers its own independent optional discard-then-draw-two.
steps.effect: Four independent instances of 'you may discard a card; if you do, draw two cards' will resolve (three copies + original), each also creating its own Wicked Role on its own target.

citations.quote: Choices that are normally made on resolution are not copied.
A copy of a spell is itself a spell, even though it has no spell card associated with it.

If an effect of a spell or ability offers any choices other than choices already made as part of casting the spell, activating the ability, or otherwise putting the spell or ability on the stack, the player announces these while applying the effect.

steps.action: You receive priority; all pass; the top copy (targeting Goblin token 3) resolves. Its target is still legal. Instructions in order: you discard a Mountain (hand 2 -> 1), so you draw two cards one at a time (hand 1 -> 3); then a Wicked Role token is created attached to Goblin token 3.
steps.effect: Hand 3 cards (1 Mountain + 2 drawn). Goblin token 3 enchanted by Wicked (+1/+1). The copy leaves the stack and ceases to exist.

citations.quote: The active player receives priority after a spell or ability (other than a mana ability) resolves.
If the spell or ability specifies targets, it checks whether the targets are still legal.
The controller of the spell or ability follows its instructions in the order written.
To discard a card, move it from its owner’s hand to that player’s graveyard.
If a player is instructed to draw multiple cards, that player performs that many individual card draws.

A Wicked Role token is a colorless Aura Role enchantment token named Wicked with enchant creature, “Enchanted creature gets +1/+1,” and “When this token is put into a graveyard from the battlefield, each opponent loses 1 life.”
If a copy of a spell is in a zone other than the stack, it ceases to exist.

steps.action: State-based actions are checked before priority: Goblin token 3 has only one Role attached, so the Role-uniqueness rule does not apply. All pass; the next copy (targeting Goblin token 2) resolves: discard (3 -> 2), draw two (2 -> 4), Wicked Role on Goblin token 2.
steps.effect: Hand 4. Goblin token 2 enchanted by Wicked. No SBA.

citations.quote: If a permanent has more than one Role controlled by the same player attached to it, each of those Roles except the one with the most recent timestamp is put into its owner’s graveyard.
When all players pass in succession, the top (last-added) spell or ability on the stack resolves.
The controller of the spell or ability follows its instructions in the order written.
If a player is instructed to draw multiple cards, that player performs that many individual card draws.

steps.action: SBA check (none). All pass; the last copy (targeting Goblin token 1) resolves: discard (4 -> 3), draw two (3 -> 5), Wicked Role on Goblin token 1.
steps.effect: Hand 5. Goblin token 1 enchanted by Wicked. No SBA.

citations.quote: When all players pass in succession, the top (last-added) spell or ability on the stack resolves.

Whenever a player would get priority (see rule 117, “Timing and Priority”), the game checks for any of the listed conditions for state-based actions, then performs all applicable state-based actions simultaneously as a single event.

steps.action: All pass; the original Witch's Mark (targeting Zada, still legal) resolves last: discard (5 -> 4), draw two (4 -> 6), Wicked Role on Zada. As the final part of resolution it is put into your graveyard.
steps.effect: Hand 6. Zada enchanted by Wicked. Stack empty. No Role SBA applies (each creature has exactly one Role). Witch's Mark and four discarded cards are in the graveyard.

citations.quote: Otherwise, the spell or ability will resolve normally.
As the final part of an instant or sorcery spell’s resolution, the spell is put into its owner’s graveyard.
If a permanent has more than one Role controlled by the same player attached to it, each of those Roles except the one with the most recent timestamp is put into its owner’s graveyard.

final_state.summary: Zada creates exactly 3 copies (one per Goblin token). Each copy and the original independently offer 'you may discard a card; if you do, draw two' (the choice is made on resolution and is not copied) and each creates its own Wicked Role on its own target. From the two Mountains in hand, discarding on every one of the four instances: 4 discards, 8 cards drawn, hand 2 -> 6 (net +4). Exactly FOUR Wicked Role tokens exist, ONE attached to each of Zada, Goblin token 1, Goblin token 2 and Goblin token 3; no creature has two Roles, so 704.5y never applies. No life changes. Assumes the library holds at least 8 cards.

graveyard: two of the drawn cards (your choice of which)
